limits: Stand-in for Google: most of this chapter's outputs on the page do not come from Google. An example marked so runs the real EZSheets library (and the real google-api-python-client) against class G, a stand-in for Google written for this course, which keeps every cell as text and parses nothing. Google was never reached, so the output shows what the library asks for and what it does with an answer, not what Google answers. The note is shown above the code of every such example, and slides of the deck that show such output say so too.

NOT EXECUTED, because no Google account, OAuth consent or Cloud project was available: every request made with an OAuth token to Google's servers. No Google account, no OAuth consent in a browser and no Google Cloud project were available, so nothing that Google answers was observed: not the creation of a spreadsheet, the title Google gives an upload, the parsing of USER_ENTERED values, the unquoted sheet title in a range, the quota errors, the content of an export, the 6 columns of the produce sheet after the upload, the Google Forms tool, the console pages and the revoking of credentials.

The chapter's printed programs were run as 47 whole programs under Python 3.14.6 with ezsheets 2026.4.28 (47 recorded runs in third_party_record_v1_0_0.json), against that stand-in at the HTTP layer or against the two public sheets read as CSV exports; a program that passes there may still fail against Google.

What Google itself answered on 2026-10-12 was only what needs no account: the three public sheets read as CSV exports (Boringcoin 27313 bytes, Bean Count 230677 bytes, both identical to the exports committed on 2026-10-01), the chapter's links, and a few requests made without credentials (the Sheets and Drive APIs answered 403 and 403). A record of one observation; web sites change and nothing re-checks it.

One ezsheets program printed the same under the seven 3.14 releases, 3.13 and 3.12 once the pickle protocol is masked (it is 5 from Python 3.14 and 4 before; recorded 2026-10-12, against the stand-in).

The page's in-browser Python is Pyodide's CPython 3.13, which has neither ezsheets nor google-api-python-client, so the page carries 14 wheels of its own (ezsheets, google_api_core, google_api_python_client, google_auth, google_auth_httplib2, google_auth_oauthlib, googleapis_common_protos, httplib2, oauthlib, proto_plus, pyasn1, pyasn1_modules, requests_oauthlib, uritemplate), downloaded from PyPI and checked by SHA-256, and loads Pyodide's own ssl, protobuf, cryptography and requests; the one change to a package is that the discovery documents of google-api-python-client other than Sheets v4 and Drive v3 were removed (no code was changed), and the page skips the docstring text that library builds for each method of each resource it creates (no request, answer or argument depends on it; without that skip an example takes several times longer in the browser), and, because the browser keeps one Python for many programs where the study ran a fresh interpreter for each, it puts ezsheets, the clock functions and the working folder back as they were at start before every program. ezsheets is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later and is embedded unmodified, with its source distribution kept beside the wheel in the repository. The page test compares every concept example's output in that browser Python with the value recorded under Python 3.14.6; six examples were changed in research version 1.0.2 where the browser cannot do what 3.14.6 did (a socket server, a second interpreter, webbrowser.get), and the unchanged record of those runs stays in the 1.0.1 files.
